name: Marsh marigold
note: Marsh marigold, Caltha palustris (docs/future/10). Drawn with the iris shader (draw: iris; flora-iris.wgsl), so its keys are the iris's, with two shapes of its own. shape.leaf kidney: each leaf is a round blade, notched where its stalk meets it, held nearly level on a stalk of the leaf height that leans out from the clump by fanDeg (the stalks spread round the clump; leafWidth is the blade's radius, arch bows the stalk outward). shape.flower cup: each flower is a cup of five rounded petals, like a buttercup, lengthShare of flowerSize long and widthShare as wide, rising riseDeg above level, their sides curling in by curl. gloss: the petals' and leaves' roughness and reflectance f0 (lit physically, so the sun catches the waxy cups; 0 roughness is matte, as the iris). A low clump of round, glossy leaves and many small golden cups on short stalks, the first strong colour of spring. habitat, growth, flowering, dormant, spread and starter work as in reeds.json: marigold wants soaked, flat ground at a pond's edge or in a marsh, wetter than iris likes and a little standing water is fine, never salt; it shuns bare rock and steep banks (the ground-type and slope axes). It flowers early, from the first days of spring, and dies back in winter. spread kind seed: its seeds float, so a mature clump drops one every everyH hours distanceM away.
